after: ! If any line printed "% Invalid" or "% Error", stop and undo it: tacctl device config plan
! dev-cisco-synthetic-vrf-stray --backout (its own region, to paste in the second terminal).
! Check now (nothing rolls this back by itself):
!   From the tacctl server:   tacctl device config pull dev-cisco-synthetic-vrf-stray --diff     (aaa, snmp and system: ok)
!   In the second terminal:   open a NEW ssh session to dev-cisco-synthetic-vrf-stray as yourself, then: terminal length 0, show privilege (must say 15)
! When both checks are fine, type this one command yourself:  write memory
! To undo: tacctl device config plan dev-cisco-synthetic-vrf-stray --backout (tacctl keeps this
! plan's back-out: after the check pull has replaced the picture, the command still prints this
! plan's, and says which pull it undoes, until the next plan with changes)
! Do not: 'write memory' before the check; paste outside the banners; paste into another device;
! paste on a console more than twenty lines at a time; keep this output in a file after the paste
! Locked out (the paste cut your session and no login works)? A superuser runs: tacctl breakglass hold dev-cisco-synthetic-vrf-stray --reason "..."
! then log in as the device's local account (console: local login, then 'enable' with the local secret),
! fix or back out, and the superuser runs: tacctl breakglass release dev-cisco-synthetic-vrf-stray

no ntp server vrf OOB ntp2.example.net
